questions.text: Why assign disjoint token-ID ranges to text, image, speech, and music codebooks in a shared vocabulary?

options.A: To let the same integer identify unrelated codes without modality information.
options.B: To ensure every modality produces exactly the same number of tokens.
options.C: To prevent collisions between modality codes in the shared ID space.
options.D: To make every modality tokenizer lossless without changing its codebook.

questions.explanation: Disjoint ranges give distinct IDs to codes from different modalities so the shared embedding and output layers can distinguish them.

questions.text: A speech system streams text tokens quickly but waits for the entire response before decoding any audio. What change directly reduces time to first audio?

options.A: Decode playable audio chunks as sufficient speech tokens arrive.
options.B: Increase the final output audio duration before starting playback.
options.C: Wait for every residual codebook token of the full response.
options.D: Measure only text-token latency and omit the audio decoder.

questions.explanation: Incremental audio decoding and playback allow the user to hear the first chunk before the complete response finishes.

questions.text: VocabSlot.end returns start + size, and build_vocab sets the next start to that end. For start=32000 and size=4096, what is the allocated ID range?
questions.explanation: The end is exclusive: [32000,36096) contains 4096 IDs, so the last valid ID is 36095 and the next slot starts at 36096.
